group: PSI Score: Pneumonia Severity Index for CAP
question:
Patient note:
A 50-year-old woman with chronic systolic ventricular dysfunction secondary to a postpartum cardiomyopathy nine years earlier and a history of stage IIA right-sided breast carcinoma treated with lumpectomy, adjuvant chemotherapy, and radiation four years ago—without evidence of recurrence on surveillance imaging this past winter—came to the emergency department late in the morning after three days of progressive shortness of breath and a new productive cough. She reports that the illness began with mild rhinorrhea and a scratchy throat during a weekend hike, but by the second evening she was panting after walking from the bedroom to the kitchen, noted streaks of blood-tinged sputum, and developed a pleuritic ache beneath the right scapula that worsened when lying on her left side. She denies dizziness, loss of consciousness, confusion, seizures, dysuria, abdominal pain, or recent antibiotic exposure. The patient works as a high-school guidance counselor, drives herself to work, and jogs at a slow pace twice weekly when well; she lives with her spouse in a single-story home and performs all activities of daily living independently. She has never been institutionalized, has had no hospital admissions for the past two years, and has not required home oxygen or diuretic up-titration since her last cardiology follow-up. Medications taken the morning of presentation include carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, sacubitril-valsartan 49-51 mg twice daily, low-dose furosemide 20 mg every other morning (skipped today), and a daily cholecalciferol supplement; she has no implanted cardiac devices or ports. She quit smoking more than twenty years ago after a 10-pack-year exposure, drinks red wine socially no more than once per week, and has never used recreational drugs. Immunizations are current, including the seasonal influenza shot given at her workplace two months earlier. Emergency medical services found her seated upright on her sofa, speaking in full sentences but tachypneic, and transported her without supplemental oxygen, intravenous fluids, or medications. On arrival to triage—and before any antipyretics, bronchodilators, antibiotics, or vasoactive agents—vital signs were temperature 36.7 °C oral, heart rate 83 beats per minute and regular, non-invasive blood pressure 132/78 mm Hg with a palpable systolic of 132 mm Hg, respiratory rate 40 breaths per minute with shallow excursions and intermittent use of sternocleidomastoids, and pulse oximetry 92 % breathing ambient air at sea level. She was alert, oriented to person, place, time, and situation, answered all questions appropriately, and followed commands without hesitation. Mucous membranes were moist; conjunctivae were anicteric. Jugular venous pulsation was noted 5 cm above the sternal angle at 45°, consistent with her cardiology baseline. Cardiac auscultation revealed a regular rhythm with a soft third heart sound but no murmurs or pericardial rub. Lung examination demonstrated markedly diminished breath sounds and stony dullness to percussion over the right posterior lower third of the thorax, with coarse crackles and egophony just superior to that zone; no wheezes were heard. The abdomen was soft and nontender with normal bowel sounds; the liver edge was not palpable. Extremities were warm without edema or cyanosis, and capillary refill was brisk. Neurologic screening showed equal, reactive pupils, fluent speech, intact cranial nerves, 5/5 strength throughout, symmetric reflexes, and steady finger-to-nose testing. A bedside finger-stick glucose registered 100 mg/dL. Venous samples and a right radial arterial puncture were obtained within ten minutes of arrival. Basic metabolic panel returned sodium 153 mEq/L, potassium 4.2 mEq/L, chloride 108 mEq/L, bicarbonate 25 mEq/L, blood urea nitrogen 11 mg/dL, and creatinine 0.8 mg/dL, consistent with her prior outpatient values. Complete blood count showed hematocrit 26 %, hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL (baseline 9.0 g/dL), leukocytes 14.8 × 10⁹/L with 87 % segmented neutrophils, and platelets 260 × 10⁹/L. An arterial blood gas on room air demonstrated pH 7.56, PaCO₂ 29 mm Hg, PaO₂ 77 mm Hg, and calculated bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, compatible with a primary respiratory alkalosis provoked by tachypnea. Serum lactate measured 1.4 mmol/L. A portable postero-anterior and lateral chest radiograph obtained before initiation of therapy revealed a dense consolidation involving the right middle lobe with air bronchograms and blunting of the adjacent costophrenic angle by a meniscus-shaped opacity suggestive of fluid accumulation; the cardiac silhouette was mildly enlarged but unchanged from an echocardiography-guided film six months prior, and there was no pulmonary vascular redistribution. Bedside thoracic ultrasonography confirmed an anechoic stripe approximately 1.2 cm thick overlying the right diaphragm consistent with a small free-flowing effusion. Electrocardiography showed normal sinus rhythm at 82–84 beats per minute, left ventricular hypertrophy voltage criteria, and T-wave flattening in the lateral leads identical to prior tracings. Two sets of blood cultures, sputum Gram stain, urinary pneumococcal and Legionella antigens, and a respiratory viral PCR panel were dispatched while the patient remained seated upright on room air. At the moment this note is drafted she has received no intravenous crystalloids, diuretics, bronchodilators, supplemental oxygen, or antimicrobial agents, thus all physiologic measurements and laboratory data above represent her untreated state on presentation.

Question: What is the patient's Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI)? You should use the patient's medical values and health status when they were first admitted to the hospital prior to any treatment.
solution:
The Pneumonia Severity Index (PSI) sums demographic, comorbidity, examination, laboratory, and radiographic points at presentation.
- Demographics: for a woman, use age minus 10: 50 − 10 = 40. No nursing-home residence = 0.
- Comorbidities: breast cancer treated within the past 5 years = 30, despite no recurrence. Heart failure from systolic cardiomyopathy = 10. No hepatic, cerebrovascular, or renal disease = 0.
- Examination: respiratory rate 40/min meets the threshold of 30/min = 20. Normal mentation, systolic pressure 132 mm Hg (not <90), temperature 36.7 °C (neither <35 nor ≥40), and pulse 83/min (not ≥125) each score 0.
- Laboratory findings: hematocrit 26% is <30% = 10. Arterial pH 7.56 is not <7.35; BUN 11 is not ≥30 mg/dL; sodium 153 is not <130 mEq/L; glucose 100 is not ≥250 mg/dL; room-air PaO₂ 77 is not <60 mm Hg. Each scores 0.
- Imaging: confirmed pleural effusion = 10.
Total = 40 + 30 + 10 + 20 + 10 + 10 = 120.
Final answer: 120
